This role is field-based, and candidates should live within the territory. This territory includes Baltimore, Bowie, South Laurel, Germantown, North Potomac, Hagerstown, Frederick, North to the border of Maryland, and the surrounding areas.
Reporting to the Senior District Manager, the Clinical Account Executive (CAE) serves as the strategic leader of their territory. They combine deep clinical expertise, strategic account planning, business acumen, and purposeful execution to improve patient outcomes, advance the organization’s mission, and support the brand objectives and business goals of the CLL and NHL Oncology Products. A CAE must be able to build trusted partnerships with customers, think like business owners, and collaborate across the oncology ecosystem to create long-term value for patients, customers, and the organization - which includes but is not limited to,  responsible resource allocation, a commitment to operating principles and compliant, high ethical standards.

SALES EXPERIENCE: Demonstrated history of delivering exceptional results through disciplined execution, accountability, and ownership. Preference for Oncology/Hematology experience.
BUSINESS ACUMEN: Thinks strategically about customers, key accounts, and market dynamics to prioritize opportunities and maximize sustainable business impact across in-field teams.
PURPOSEFUL EXECUTION: Consistently translates strategy into focused action, balancing urgency with discipline while executing with precision.
LEARNING AGILITY: Rapidly learns complex scientific, clinical, and business concepts and confidently applies them in dynamic customer environments.
COMMUNICATION: Simplifies complex clinical and business concepts into clear, compelling points.
RESILIENCE: Demonstrates grit, adaptability, and persistence while maintaining a positive, solutions-oriented approach in a competitive environment.
INTELLECTUAL CURIOSITY: Naturally seeks to understand the science, the customer, and the business beyond what is required.
Develop and execute a comprehensive territory business plan aligned with brand strategy and local customer needs.
Build trusted relationships with hematologists, oncologists, nurses, pharmacists, administrators, and key account stakeholders.
Demonstrate deep scientific and clinical expertise while delivering compliant, customer-focused engagements.
Partner effectively with cross-functional colleagues to deliver coordinated customer experiences.

description:
About AbbVie

We are seeking a Principal Research Scientist I to join the Bioassay Development team within our Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) organization. This Principal Research Scientist I will support the development and evaluation of newly discovered oncology and immunology drugs and existing clinical candidates, including antibody therapeutics, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), multi-specific biologics, and other complex novel biologic modalities.
This role is within a team of highly experienced scientists and managers who have directly enabled the development/IND submissions of numerous novel oncology drugs, as well as successfully filed BLAs. In this role you will have unique exposure to a significant breadth and depth of drug development experience, numerous cross-functional interactions, and opportunities to grow and develop in your career.
Responsibilities:
In this lab-based role, and as a potency assay subject matter expert (SME) and senior scientist in the group, your major responsibilities will include:
Leading the development and optimization of novel, custom, complex cell-based functional potency assays (bioassays) and target-binding potency assays critical to the development of new oncology and immunology biologic drugs within a Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) organization.
Leading the innovation, exploration, and development of new potency assay techniques, approaches, technologies, and strategies.
Training, mentoring, supporting, and supervising team members
Performing complex troubleshooting and optimization experiments
Representing the Bioassay Development group cross-functionally and externally
Presenting your work at internal and external scientific events.
Executing biological activity characterization experiments to support drug development activities and IND submissions.
Working directly with other functional areas of the CMC Biologics - Analytical Development team (= Quality Control, Separations & Compendials, Process Analytics, Mass Spec, and Analytical Leads) on complex structure/function molecular characterization.

Provide functional leadership across Normal, Expedited, Emergency, and Standard Change processes.
Lead structured reviews of change records for completeness, quality, risk, readiness, and alignment with process requirements.
Identify and address unauthorized, latent, urgent, miscategorized, or otherwise non-compliant changes, escalating material or recurring concerns as appropriate.
Analyze recurring process and change-quality issues and recommend improvements to governance, guidance, training, controls, or system capabilities.

Partner with change owners, technical teams, and technology leaders to resolve readiness or documentation gaps before governance review.

Coordinate Post-Implementation Review activities for applicable changes, including candidate identification, completion tracking, stakeholder follow-up, and documentation of outcomes.
Analyze failed changes, PIR outcomes, and recurring quality or compliance issues to identify systemic trends and opportunities for corrective or preventive improvement.

Develop, maintain, and enhance Change Management reports, dashboards, metrics, and recurring operational summaries.
Analyze trends in change performance, including change success, aging records, failed changes, PIR activity, process compliance, and change-quality indicators.
Translate operational data into actionable insights and recommendations for Change Management leadership, technology teams, and governance stakeholders.
Partner with ServiceNow, Service Management, Quality, and process stakeholders to define and support Change Management enhancements, including requirements, testing, validation, communication, and adoption.
Identify opportunities to simplify or automate recurring reporting, notifications, workflow activities, and operational follow-up.
Support the continued modernization, governance, and recertification of Standard Changes and identification of repeatable activities appropriate for Standard Change.

Maintain and improve Change Management knowledge articles, procedures, job aids, standards, and supporting process documentation.
Ensure Change Management documentation remains aligned with current ServiceNow workflows, approval models, governance requirements, and operating practices.
Develop communications, guidance, and training materials supporting process changes and recurring change-quality needs.
Serve as a trusted Change Management advisor to technical teams, Service Management, Quality, governance partners, and business stakeholders.
Provide clear guidance on Change Management requirements, change readiness, documentation, approvals, governance expectations, and ServiceNow usage.
Influence cross-functional stakeholders to address identified risks and process gaps and escalate significant or recurring concerns when appropriate.

ITIL Foundation certification or advanced ITIL/IT Service Management certification.

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred
Ability to coordinate activities and work simultaneously on multiple projects, in a global, fast-paced setting where priorities may change quickly.

Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.

title: Sr Scientist, Quantitative Bioimaging
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
We are seeking a Senior Scientist to advance quantitative bioimaging capabilities in support of immunology discovery research. In this role, you will work within a cross-functional team with access to multiple microscopy modalities, complex in vitro models, multimodal biological datasets, and advanced computational infrastructure.
You will develop and apply quantitative imaging, computer-vision, and machine-learning approaches to characterize cellular and tissue phenotypes, support the development of biological models, including co-cultures, organ-on-chip systems, organoids, and tissue explants, and generate insights that advance immunology discovery programs. This role combines hands-on delivery of robust, reproducible image-analysis workflows with the evaluation and application of advanced AI/ML approaches, including biomedical image segmentation, representation learning, foundation models, and scalable computational workflows. You will partner closely with wet-lab scientists, imaging specialists, computational scientists, and other subject-matter experts to translate biological questions into rigorous and impactful analysis strategies.
The role sits at the intersection of biology, bioengineering, microscopy, and computational science. Candidates with combined expertise in two or more of these areas are especially encouraged to apply.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, optimize, and apply imaging assays and quantitative image-analysis workflows for 2D and 3D cellular and tissue models to characterize cellular and other complex biological phenotypes.
Collaborate with wet-lab assay scientists, imaging specialists, and computational scientists from experimental and assay design through image acquisition, analysis, validation, and data delivery.
Extract biologically meaningful, multiparametric features from high-content imaging datasets and use them to characterize disease-relevant phenotypes, mechanisms, and treatment responses.
Apply statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods to identify candidate imaging biomarkers and relate imaging phenotypes to molecular, functional, and other biological readouts.
Contribute to the integration of imaging data with multimodal datasets, including molecular, single-cell, spatial, or perturbational data, where appropriate.
Establish quality-control and evaluation frameworks to assess image and assay quality, distinguish biological signal from technical artifacts, and define data-quality criteria, acceptance thresholds, and analytical limitations.
Maintain clear experimental and analytical records; analyze, visualize, and present results rigorously to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Communicate methods, assumptions, results, uncertainties, and limitations effectively to cross-functional project teams.
Stay current with advances in quantitative bioimaging, image analysis, computer vision, and AI/ML for biological imaging, and evaluate opportunities to incorporate relevant approaches into team workflows.
Basic Qualifications
BS, MS, or PhD in engineering, biophysics, computational biology, imaging science, bioinformatics, or a related discipline, with typically 10-12+ (BS), 8-10+ (MS), or 0-4+ (PhD) years experience.
Demonstrated experience developing quantitative image-analysis or computational solutions involving one or more of the following: image segmentation, feature extraction, phenotypic profiling, object classification, or analysis of high-content imaging data.
Experience with at least one relevant imaging modality or assay type, such as confocal microscopy, high-content imaging, or cell painting.
Ability to assess image quality, recognize common imaging artifacts, and interpret biologically meaningful phenotypes.
Working knowledge of machine-learning or deep-learning approaches for biological imaging, with the ability to understand model behavior, assess performance, and contribute to appropriate evaluation strategies.
Proficiency with the Python data-science ecosystem, including NumPy, pandas, Polars, scikit-learn, and/or PyTorch.
Strong biological grounding, attention to experimental rigor, and demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with wet-lab and computational colleagues.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain methods, results, assumptions, and limitations to diverse audiences.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience working with complex in vitro models, such as organoids, organ-on-chip systems, co-cultures, tissue explants, or other advanced in vitro platforms.
Experience with classical bioimage-analysis tools such as CellProfiler, scikit-image, ImageJ/Fiji, or comparable platforms.
Exposure to deep-learning, self-supervised learning, foundation-model, embedding-based, or multimodal AI approaches for biological imaging.
Peer-reviewed publications, patents, conference presentations, or other demonstrated scientific contributions in quantitative bioimaging, computer vision, computational biology, bioengineering, or a related field.
Position will be filled at level commensurate with extent of education, experience, and accomplishment— Senior Scientist I or Senior Scientist II

description:
About the Role
The Global Alliance Director, AWS owns the strategic partnership between Adobe and AWS. You will set and execute the joint go-to-market (GTM) strategy, expand customer relationships and AWS Marketplace adoption, and align executives, field teams, product, and marketing across both companies. As the primary liaison between Adobe and AWS, you are accountable for revenue growth, cloud adoption, seller enablement, and delivery of the joint business plan.
This is a build role. AWS’s partner ecosystem is early, and its programs are still being designed. You will work across AWS, technology partners, and systems integrators (SIs), whose incentives on any given deal don’t always align, and you will help shape how new technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy and Execution
Own the end-to-end GTM strategy and operation of the alliance, prioritizing high-value enterprise opportunities and driving revenue through AWS field engagement and joint co-sell motions.
Decide where to concentrate investment across the partner portfolio, and make the case to stop investing where returns are not there.
Provide market intelligence and competitive insight on the partner ecosystem to inform product and commercial strategy.
Partner with Adobe’s alliances, sales, partner marketing, and regional cloud teams to keep the motion consistent globally while regions execute locally.
Governance and Operating Cadence
Lead the alliance operating rhythm: annual business planning, executive business reviews (EBRs), and quarterly and monthly business reviews (QBRs, MBRs).
Develop and manage annual business plans, growth initiatives, and partnership objectives with Adobe and AWS leaders.
Build scalable processes for partnership operations, including escalation management, business reviews, and reporting.
Maintain executive engagement plans, stakeholder maps, governance frameworks, and action tracking.
Prepare executive-ready materials, including strategic updates, account reviews, business cases, win stories, and operating plans.

Own executive dashboards, scorecards, pipeline reviews, forecasting, and performance reporting for both leadership teams.
Define, track, and report alliance KPIs: revenue influence, AWS consumption, Marketplace performance, co-sell activity, customer adoption, migration outcomes, and executive engagement.
Monitor partnership health, flag risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to accelerate growth, drawing on data from sales, finance, marketing, product, engineering, and customer success.
Drive operational excellence through process improvement, reporting automation, and business insights.
Field Activation and Marketplace Growth
Expand AWS Marketplace adoption and manage incentive programs, sponsorships, funding, and co-sell benefits.
Activate partner field teams around Adobe priorities and strategic accounts to accelerate adoption of Adobe’s priority joint solutions and relevant third-party partner solutions.
Deliver enablement programs, workshops, and GTM guidance so Adobe solutions are positioned effectively in AWS customer conversations, driving consumption through Adobe workloads and modern workplace initiatives.
Support regional sales leadership meetings, pipeline management, reporting, and field enablement alongside the Adobe AWS Alliance team.
Marketing and Thought Leadership
Work with Adobe and AWS sales and marketing teams to develop assets, events, and customer programs.
Support customer references, success stories, analyst engagements, and executive communications.
Present at industry events, customer workshops, and alliance forums, positioning Adobe as a strategic cloud, AI, and digital workspace partner in the AWS ecosystem.
Cross-Functional and Product Alignment
Align executives, product teams, the Adobe-AWS partner team, sales leadership, and marketing around year-over-year revenue growth.
Coordinate stakeholders across sales, marketing, product, engineering, finance, and operations to drive accountability on strategic initiatives.
Work with product management and engineering to align Adobe and AWS roadmaps and secure opportunities and funding for integration, innovation, and joint solutions.
Represent customer and AWS requirements in product planning, using adoption metrics and usage telemetry to measure impact and business value.

Education: MBA or equivalent practical experience.
Experience: 15+ years in global technology partner management, GTM, and partner sales leadership, working directly with enterprise customers, cloud service providers, C-level executives, and sales leaders.
Industry knowledge: Enterprise software sales and operations, competitive landscapes, and cloud marketplace business models.
Alliance expertise: Deep knowledge of alliance management, co-sell metrics and motions, and partner programs, ideally within the AWS ecosystem.
Hyperscaler partnerships: Experience developing GTM strategy and co-sell programs with the largest hyperscalers.
Strategic agreements: Experience planning and executing multi-year partner sales and product agreements.

Communication: Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.

title: Deployment Program Manager, Global Logistics
description:
At Amazon, we are deploying Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) tracking technology across our physical network in a first-of-its-kind effort — at a scale and in a way that has not been done anywhere else in the company. This initiative brings real-time, item-level visibility to inbound shipments, and getting the underlying infrastructure installed and live across many sites is the critical path to making it real.
As a Deployment Program Manager, you own the end-to-end execution of site-based infrastructure deployment — from site survey through installation, testing, and go-live — coordinating internal Amazon stakeholders (IT, Operations, Reliability & Maintenance Engineering, and Site Points of Contact) and external installation partners across multiple concurrent sites. This is a tactical, hands-on execution role focused on driving sites through the deployment pipeline. You will be based in Los Angeles and travel to sites as needed for critical milestones, safety reviews, and partner relationship-building.
Key job responsibilities
• Drive parallel pre-install workstreams — network/IT readiness, safety and compliance documentation, hardware procurement and staging, and operational readiness — to completion before installation windows are committed.
• Serve as the primary field coordination point between installation vendors, site points of contact, and internal Amazon teams during active installs.
• Provide timely, accurate site-level status input (survey, design, network readiness, installation, and go-live milestones) to the program’s reporting process.
• Escalate blockers in real time — access delays, compliance gaps, scheduling conflicts, equipment issues — to protect the program’s delivery timeline.
• Coordinate site readiness planning pre-install, including safety zones, operational vs. non-operational area access, and daily coordination plans with site operations.
• Support post-installation testing and validation coordination with technology and installation partners.
• Maintain and continuously improve deployment playbooks and pre-install checklists based on site-by-site lessons learned.
• Travel to sites as needed for critical milestones, safety reviews, and stakeholder relationship-building (frequency determined by program needs).
A day in the life
Your day balances two kinds of work. For sites approaching installation, you run proactive, scheduled readiness coordination — kickoff calls with the Site POC, site IT, and the vendor; dedicated IT follow-up on network readiness; vendor and safety/compliance prep; and a final go/no-go on the start date. For sites already in active installation, you shift to reactive, real-time troubleshooting — morning check-ins, ad hoc issue calls, same-day escalation of field blockers, and feeding site-level status into the program’s reporting. Periodic site travel and ongoing refinement of the deployment playbook round out the role.
About the team
You are part of Global Logistics which provides transportation offerings from imports and domestic shippers into the Amazon Warehouse and Distribution and Fulfillment Network. We treat our shippers as customers and obsess with giving them a loveable way to inject their inventory into our network. In this team specifically, this is a first-of-its-kind initiative bringing Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) tracking technology to Amazon’s physical network to deliver real-time, item-level visibility into inbound shipments. The deployment team is responsible for bringing this infrastructure online across sites — partnering with Operations, IT, Reliability & Maintenance Engineering, site leadership, and external installation vendors to turn the technology vision into live, working capability on the floor. It is a fast-moving, high-ownership environment where field execution directly determines how quickly the program scales.

- 3+ years of maintenance planner/scheduler in industrial maintenance, manufacturing, or distribution industries experience

- Experience in MS Access and SQL
- Experience in requirement gathering and ability to write clear and detailed requirement document
- Experience using Microsoft Projects software
- Experience with material handling systems (MHS) installation, operation and maintenance
- Experience working in an analytical environment with cross-functional teams

title: Inventory Health Program Lead, Materials Allocation & Planning
description:
AWS runs the largest cloud infrastructure in the world, backed by billions of dollars in hardware inventory. We’re looking for an Inventory Health Program Lead to turn excess and obsolete (E&O) hardware into value. You’ll build secondary supply channels that don’t exist at scale today, structure commercial deals with suppliers and partners, and work with hardware engineering to qualify excess parts into current and future builds. This is a 2–3 year effort across every commodity family. The long-term goal is to change how AWS sources and commits to hardware, so E&O exposure is prevented upstream instead of cleaned up afterward.
In this role, you will:
Build a program from scratch that owns the full lifecycle of inventory health — from proactive exposure monitoring and inspection through financial alignment, cost recovery, and commercial disposition. Establish governance, standardized processes, and executive review cadences across a global network of integrator and ODM sites spanning multiple commodity families.
Drive measurable outcomes tied directly to financial planning cycles, with reduction targets tracked monthly, quarterly, and annually. Own the automation roadmap that replaces manual, fragmented workflows with scalable, system-driven execution
This isn't a role where you inherit a playbook — you're writing it. You'll work across engineering, finance, operations, and manufacturing partners to bring structure and accountability to a space with massive impact on AWS's cost structure. If you thrive on ambiguity, love building from zero, and want your work to be visible at the highest levels of the organization, this is the role.
Key job responsibilities
Design, negotiate and scale new reuse, resale and recovery channels, including secondary-market buyers, ODM/integrator buy-backs and cross-platform redeployment.
Structure strategic buy transactions with suppliers and partners on excess positions, covering returns, rebalancing and repurposing.
Work with hardware engineering to qualify excess components into current and future platforms through BOM cross-referencing and fungibility analysis, shaping platform design and sourcing decisions.
Feed recovery insights back into category strategy so future sourcing and commitment decisions reduce E&O exposure.
Own a multi-year E&O reduction strategy across all commodity families, with targets built into OP1/OP2 and tracked monthly, quarterly and annually.
Set up the governance, standard disposition processes and executive review cadences that support channel execution across global integrator and ODM sites.
Define the automation roadmap and KPIs that show leadership how much is being recovered, how fast cycles are moving and where the risk is.
A day in the life
Negotiating terms with a secondary-market buyer or an ODM on a buy-back of excess material.
Working through a BOM cross-reference with hardware engineering to qualify excess parts for a new platform build.
Modeling the recovery value of different disposition paths (redeploy, resell, return, write off) and taking a recommendation to Finance.
Partnering with commodity managers to change commit strategy based on where exposure keeps building up.
Presenting channel performance and E&O reduction progress to senior leadership
About the team
You'll join a team within AWS Infrastructure Supply Chain that ensures the right hardware is planned, allocated, and positioned across one of the largest global supply chains in the world. This role stands up a new commercial function focused on recovering value from hardware inventory. You'll have the autonomy to build new channels and the visibility to shape how AWS sources hardware. We own the end-to-end material lifecycle — from supply planning and allocation through inventory health management across a global network of manufacturing sites. We build from zero, operate at massive scale with startup energy, and sit at the center of engineering, finance, and operations. Every person has outsized impact. This role stands up a new function focused on inventory health — you'll have the autonomy to build it and the visibility to drive change.
Basic qualifications: - 5+ years of relevant strategic sourcing including vendor negotiations, global contract management, process improvement, operational and financial analysis experience
- 5+ years of program or project management experience, or a MBA and 5+ years of working cross functionally across several teams experience
- Experience presenting to both technical and non-technical executive audiences

What You Will Do
You will own how a new Storage platform is manufactured. You will run NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments before design freeze, lead design reviews, and drive root cause corrective action on manufacturing blockers and quality escapes. When a platform ramps to volume with high first-pass yield and no quality escapes reaching the fleet, that is your impact.
Why You Will Love It
The world's most advanced frontier models train on the hardware you help build. You will see your process and test decisions scale across a large fleet of servers, and you will work at the point where design meets the factory floor. The team is deeply technical and high-trust, and you own manufacturing outcomes end to end from design engagement through volume production.

You think across the full manufacturing stack, from SMT assembly and test coverage to line balance, yield, and quality systems. You are as comfortable in a DFx review reading gerber files as you are on an ODM floor debugging a failing test station. You drive decisions with data, hold manufacturing partners to a high bar, and bring structured problem-solving and disciplined change management to a fast-moving NPI environment. You mentor junior engineers, contribute to hiring, and raise the manufacturing engineering bar for the team.

Design for Manufacturability & Risk

Quality & Continuous Improvement
- Drive Root Cause Corrective Action (RCCA) for manufacturing blockers and quality escapes

- Own manufacturing quality metrics and drive yield improvement, and cost optimization through process and automation engineering
Capacity & Production Ramp

- Provide on-site ODM support during critical builds and production ramp
- Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams on Storage module integration, thermal validation, and manufacturing requirements
Cross-Team Collaboration

- Domestic and international travel (~25%) to ODM/CM and design partner sites

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Shipping Speed, Selection & Charges, Shipping Platform
description:
Every time someone shops on Amazon, our systems influence what they see about delivery: whether an item can ship to them, how fast it will arrive, and what shipping will cost. We own shipping speed, selection and charges for Amazon stores around the world. Our 6 Tier-1 services sit on the critical path of every product page, cart and checkout, handling millions of requests per second before checkout. We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help us modernize how that works and to change how we build software along the way.
You'll lead three programs that matter to customers and to how we build:
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilities. Our ship options were first built just to describe speed. Over time each one also took on other delivery features, so a single identifier now does several jobs across many ordering, delivery and fulfillment systems. You'll drive the multi-year platform change that lets teams launch new delivery experiences, like ultra-fast quick commerce, age-verified delivery or grocery delivery, by combining reusable building blocks. Today each one needs a new ship option.
Build the customer rescue product. When an item can't be delivered to a customer, the purchase shouldn't end there. Our team is building customer rescue, the product that catches these dead ends across the shopping journey and help customers complete their order: healing carts and checkouts with substitutes and alternate offers and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery. You'll drive its delivery and adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce and other programs, partnering with the teams who own each experience.
Help lead our move to AI-driven software development. We're building toward a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in where human judgment matters. You'll own the plan to roll this out across our teams, decide how we measure success.
You'll work with principal engineers, product managers and engineering leaders across Amazon, and you'll regularly write for and present to senior leadership.
Key job responsibilities
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilites
Own the roadmap to move Amazon's ordering and delivery systems off ship-option-specific logic and onto reusable capabilities and signals, so new delivery experiences launch without new ship options.
Drive adoption across shipping, checkout, fulfillment and transportation systems. Sequence integrations, align designs with principal and senior engineers, and onboard new businesses such as quick commerce, grocery and age-verified delivery.
Customer rescue product
Drive delivery of the customer rescue product from roadmap to launch: cart and checkout healing with substitutes and alternate offers, clear restriction messages, and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery.
Lead adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce, partnering with the teams who own each shopping experience.
Coordinate A/B experiments, staged rollouts and launch readiness across marketplaces, and use the results to drive launch decisions.
Run weekly, monthly and business reviews with senior leadership, with written narratives on results, risks, recovery plans and decisions needed.
AI-driven software development
Own the plan to move our teams to a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in at key decision points. Push for full adoption over isolated pilots.
Define how adoption and impact are measured, such as coverage by service, changes shipped through agents and automated test coverage.
A day in the life
Your morning might start chairing the Ship Option Control Board, where you and principal engineers from several organizations decide whether a new delivery experience should be a reusable capability or a signal. Later you turn the latest customer rescue experiment readout into a clear recommendation for the weekly leadership review, then meet with a partner team to plan bringing the product into their shopping experience. In the afternoon you sit with a team moving its service to AI-driven development, find where the agents still get stuck, and fold those gaps into the adoption plan. You might end the day tuning an agent that drafts your program update from tracker data, so the next one takes minutes instead of hours.

title: Embedded Software Engineer - Always On Platforms, Core OS

At Apple, the Always-On Processor (AOP) firmware team builds the software that runs on that silicon. We write the firmware that listens to the world through accelerometers, gyroscopes, barometers, magnetometers, and more, while sipping just microwatts of power.
Our work sits underneath features people rely on every day, from emergency response and fitness tracking to camera image stabilization, spatial audio, intuitive device interactions, and all-day battery life. Experience in Si characterization and debug.

title: Senior Engineering Manager - Apple Cloud Storage Infrastructure

title: Software Developement Manager, Apple Services Engineering
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center, with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements.
We're starting a new team focused on one question: how do we patch the node software across our datacenter fleet faster, and more often, with minimal impact to the workloads running on it? We're looking for a domain expert to decide the approach and then build and lead the team that delivers it.
Today, updating a node's software means choosing between speed and workload impact. This team's job is to remove that tradeoff, so we can patch the fleet faster and more often with minimal impact on users. We have not chosen an approach. Live migration, snapshot and restore, kexec-based host updates, live patching, and in-place upgrade of the runtime and VMM are all options, and a different approach may fit better than any of them. We are looking for an expert to decide and guide: which approach, or combination, gets us there, what it costs in workload impact and operational risk, and how we measure the result.
You will:
* Define the fleet patching strategy: evaluate the candidate approaches (including ones we haven't listed), choose, and make the tradeoffs explicit, grounded in a model of how each one fails.
* Set the metrics that matter, such as guest-visible downtime, total migration time, network amplification, abortability, and time to patch the fleet.
* Design and drive the first implementation, building on Cloud Hypervisor and our Linux microVM runtimes on x86 and arm64.
* Hire and grow the team. Depending on your background and interests this is a technical-lead role or a people-management role, and we will decide that together.
* Work with the SRE, Compute, and security organizations on rollout, safety, and fleet operations.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, or equivalent related experience.
At least 8+ years of software design and development experience in infrastructure engineering (compute, storage and network virtualization).
Deep, demonstrated experience in one of the following, and working fluency in the other:
* Operating live migration, live patching, or kexec-style host updates across a production fleet, including the failures: non-convergence, aborts and rollback, and fleet-wide rollout safety.
* Building live migration, snapshot/restore, or device-state serialization inside a hypervisor or VMM (for example QEMU/KVM, Cloud Hypervisor, Firecracker, Xen, or Hyper-V).
Advanced programming language proficiency in C, C++, Rust, Swift or Go, with a track record of designing and developing high performance, secured, scalable and reliable systems.
Track record of owning technical design end-to-end, from design docs and architecture tradeoffs through implementation and review.
Experience setting technical direction for a group of engineers, with or without formal management responsibility.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with Linux kernel and system programming (KVM, userfaultfd, VFIO, kexec, kernel live patching).
Understanding of dirty-page tracking, memory and device state handling, and time and CPU-model compatibility across hosts.
Experience with live migration of devices that carry hardware state (VFIO, vDPA, SR-IOV).
Experience designing benchmarks and load tests to characterize downtime and performance impact during an upgrade.

title: Wireless RF OTA MIMO Systems Engineer
description:
At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet? Do you like changing the game? As a Wireless RF OTA MIMO Systems Engineer, you will have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape upcoming products that will delight and inspire millions of Apple’s customers every day. Apple's Wireless Systems team is looking for an engineer to develop the test systems and methodologies that characterize over-the-air performance across different wireless technologies for Apple's wireless products.
In this role, you will own the methodology behind our radiated MIMO measurements. You will design and verify OTA test systems that reproduce real-world propagation environments in the lab, develop test strategies for new wireless features as they come to market, and turn measurement data into clear insights about device performance. You will partner closely with cross-functional teams to find and resolve system-level issues early in the product cycle, and your work will directly influence design decisions across Apple’s wireless products.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in EE or equivalent with 10+ years of relevant work experience.
Strong technical background in wireless communication, including wireless protocols, antennas, and radio propagation.
Working experience with MIMO characteristics (at a system level), antenna design and requirements for modern wireless communication systems such as LTE, 5G NR (FR1/FR2) and Wi-Fi.
Strong problem solving and analytical skills.
Strong programming skills (MATLAB/Python).
Preferred qualifications: Master’s Degree in EE or equivalent with 10+ years of relevant work experience.
Working experience with different lab equipment: network analyzers, signal generators, signal analyzers, call boxes, channel emulators.
Experience with OTA test systems such as multi-probe anechoic chambers (MPAC), radiated two-stage (RTS), or reverberation chambers.
Familiarity with regulatory requirements and certification process for CTIA and 3GPP, including MIMO OTA test methodologies.
Experience with post-processing techniques and algorithms for extracting MIMO channel characterization metrics and other key performance indicators.
Knowledge of spatial channel models and their implementation in channel emulators.
Experience building test automation and data analysis pipelines.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work across hardware, software, and program teams.

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Maintenance Planner to keep our facilities and production line equipment running. You'll plan preventive maintenance, schedule repairs, track parts, and make sure the right technician has the right job at the right time. This role resides within the maintenance/facilities team — if a line goes down, or output stops, your planning is what keeps things moving.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and maintain preventive maintenance schedules for facilities systems (HVAC, electrical, building infrastructure) and production line equipment

 - Turn maintenance requests into work orders — prioritize by urgency, safety, and impact on production

 - Track parts and spares inventory for production equipment, and order what's needed before it runs out

 - Coordinate with technicians, vendors, and outside contractors to schedule work around production schedules with minimal downtime

 - Maintain accurate records in the CMMS (computerized maintenance management system) work orders, asset history, downtime

 - Track maintenance costs and flag equipment that's costing more to fix than replace

 - Run weekly planning meetings with maintenance and production leads to review backlog and upcoming work




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 3+ years in maintenance planning or scheduling, ideally in a manufacturing or production environment

 - Experience with a CMMS (MaintainX, Maximo, SAP, or similar)

 - Comfortable reading equipment manuals and basic mechanical/electrical schematics

 - Strong organizational skills; juggling many work orders and know which one matters most today

 - Clear communicator; you'll be the point of contact between technicians, vendors, and production leaders

 - Equipment spare parts BOM experience

 - Spare parts crib management knowledge




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Facilities and Maintenance team is responsible for keeping Base Factory 1 running safely, reliably, and efficiently every hour of every shift. As Base scales production of home battery systems, this team builds the maintenance programs, reliability systems, and facility infrastructure that prevent downtime before it happens and enable manufacturing to meet growing customer demand. You'll have the opportunity to establish the foundation for a world-class maintenance organization—from preventive maintenance and spare parts strategy to equipment reliability and facility operations—rather than inheriting legacy systems. If you're excited by the challenge of building systems from the ground up, solving complex operational problems, and seeing the direct impact of your work on production output, quality, and company growth, this is a rare opportunity to shape the future of a rapidly scaling factory.

****EOE, including disability/vets**** Cox Fleet keeps your fleet moving.
Headquartered in Indianapolis, Cox Fleet has grown to become one of the largest fleet maintenance companies in the country.
Cox Fleet is the leading provider of on-site mobile maintenance and repair services nationwide, offering mobile on-site fleet service for light medium, and heavy-duty trucks and trailers. Cox Fleet also services customers utilizing its 20+ nationwide service centers; each offering accident repair, painting, refurbishment, and heavy mechanical repair. We are supported by a 24/7 in-house call center and provide scheduled maintenance services and unscheduled services to fleets anywhere, anytime.
Have you ever thought about a career as a Diesel Technician?
Are you tired of working hard at a dead-end J-O-B and no appreciation for your contributions?
Do you want to feel proud of what you do and get on the path to a better and brighter future for you and your family?
Did you take apart and put back together that pickup truck in your driveway? Does your compact have an exhaust pipe that is way too loud and a spoiler with enough down force to keep you driving under the speed limit? (Looks nice though).
Are you working as a lube tech or other position in the maintenance shop, but your company does not provide education or tools?
FleeTec Academy is a  paid educational program that leads to becoming one of our full time Diesel & Trailer Technicians.  It was established by us to help people get into Diesel & Trailer Maintenance field who otherwise might not be able to afford to spend over a year of their life at an expensive formal Technical School with all the associated tuition debt and buy all the necessary tools for the job without maxing out their credit card.
That’s right, we pay you to go through our program, we give you free education on fundamentals of Diesel Engines and how to fix trucks, along with a set of hand tools with toolbox, to get you on your way to be the best Diesel & Trailer Technician out there!
Sounds too good to be true. What is the catch, right? Here is what we ask from you in return: You must be willing to study hard (and we mean HARD!) for ten (10) weeks of full-time schooling at our Academy Campus. Travel expenses are paid by us, along with hotel accommodation and stipend for meals, plus a weekly paycheck. Upon completion of the initial classroom phase, you will be paired up with a Lead Technician in your market for further hands-on training and offered an actual full-time job with us! You will be sent back for another 5 week of further classroom study to keep developing your skill set, and upon successful completion of the full multi-year program, you will be able to call yourself a Diesel Technician! Oh, and keep the tools.
To summarize:
5 weeks paid classroom training in Indianapolis, IN, all travel expenses paid. 8 to 10 weeks of mentorship in the field back home; followed by another 5 weeks paid classroom training in Indianapolis.
Free Technical Education
Further hands-on training by one of our technicians and a full-time job with us as a Mobile Diesel Mechanic in your market.
Our Mobile Technicians are assigned a state-of-the-art vehicle, with all the bells and whistles, which they use to perform vehicle repairs at our customers’ locations. You are not going to be doing emergency truck repairs on a side of the road as part of your everyday duties, but rather go to our customers’ locations to do preventative maintenance and general repairs onsite, so they can keep their vehicles running efficiently without having to take them to the shop.

About the Team
We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps.
About the Role
As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.
You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you...
Thrive on iteration and have experience leading teams through changes
Are excited about coaching, managing, and leading teams in fast-paced environments
Enjoy building systems and processes and seeing ideas come to life
Are eager to learn how different parts of a complex operation connect
Are obsessed with preparing consistent, high-quality food for customers
Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations
You’ll Make an Impact By...
Leading: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Kitchen Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. Because this position supervises staff and is responsible for maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, strong adherence to professional conduct, clear communication, and employee safety standards is required. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your DMK, helping your team to navigate new food concepts and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operating and Building Systems: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results for your kitchen. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success by building, implementing, and improving systems for effective scheduling, ensuring par levels are met, executing recipes accurately, and deploying best practices.Because this role oversees high-risk kitchen equipment and fast-paced food production, maintaining sound judgment and unimpaired performance is essential to ensure a safe work environment. You’ll engage cross-functional partners within DoorDash as needed for support.
Strategizing: You will analyze performance metrics, identify root causes of issues like prep gaps or order quality, and implement solutions that drive efficiency and adoption. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates.
Delighting: You care deeply about delivering great food and a great customer experience. You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You will collaborate with central teams so your site has the tools, training, and support needed to achieve excellent quality outcomes.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 3+ years of experience in a medium/high-volume fast-casual or full-service restaurant environment.
You have 2+ years of experience leading teams, including hiring, scheduling, coaching, and performance management.
You hold (or are willing to get) a ServeSafe Manager certification and set high standards for food safety and cleanliness.
You’re a hands-on leader who motivates teams of 5+ employees to perform and grow.
You take ownership and thrive in fast-changing, startup-style environments where no task is too big or small.
You’re a creative problem solver who challenges “how it’s always been done” and finds better ways forward.
You’re analytical, data-driven, and comfortable using Excel or Google Sheets to make decisions.
As the leader of the site, you will need to ensure your team and the site is fully supported, which will include regularly scheduled late-night and weekend hours.
You’re comfortable flexing between kitchen and fulfillment operations, and you understand how culinary execution and order flow connect to overall site metrics like accuracy, quality, and efficiency.
You have (or can quickly learn) a working knowledge of inventory management systems (IMS), product flow, and fulfillment best practices within a multi-operation site.

We are leaders - Leadership is not limited to our management team. It’s something everyone at DoorDash embraces and embodies.
We are doers - We believe the only way to predict the future is to build it. Creating solutions that will lead our company and our industry is what we do -- on every project, every day.
We are learners - We’re not afraid to dig in and uncover the truth, even if it’s scary or inconvenient. Everyone here is continually learning on the job, no matter if we’ve been in a role for one year or one minute.

title: Senior Full Stack & Platform Engineer
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
About Compass
Compass is a new venture incubated within MISUMI Americas. We’re building it with the deep manufacturing expertise of Fictiv, MISUMI’s digital manufacturing platform.
Every physical product starts as a CAD model, and most of what it will cost is decided right there. Yet cost and manufacturability are still checked after the drawings are released, by hand and in spreadsheets, when every change is slow and expensive. The result is redesigns, missed schedules, and money left on the factory floor. Compass fixes that at the source. An engineer uploads an assembly, and Compass reads every part the way an expert manufacturing engineer would. It checks each feature against the processes that could make it, prices the part at the volume that matters, reads tolerances and GD&T straight off the drawing, and ranks exactly what to change. It does this across the entire bill of materials, reruns on every revision, and learns from every correction engineers make.
The problems underneath are genuinely hard: making sense of real-world geometry, modeling cost across machining, casting, molding, sheet metal, and additive, interpreting engineering drawings, and building AI that gets measurably better from expert feedback. The stakes are real, too. Our customers are enterprise engineering teams, including aerospace and defense programs, where the platform has to be as secure and trustworthy as it is smart. Compass is a small team that moves fast and gives engineers real ownership. You won’t inherit a finished system. You’ll help define the architecture, the security foundation, and the product that the most demanding customers in manufacturing will rely on.
About the Role
We’re looking for a cross-functional software engineer who thrives at the intersection of application development and cloud infrastructure. We’re scaling the product, fast-tracking SOC 2 Type I and Type II, and building an ITAR-ready environment for aerospace and defense customers. You’ll be one of the engineers who makes all three happen.
We don’t need a pure DevOps specialist managing servers all day. We need an engineer who treats infrastructure as code, automates our cloud environment to satisfy security audits, and writes clean application code to ship features customers use.
You’ll own our AWS infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines. In your first months, much of your time will go to building our compliance foundation. Over time, the role settles into roughly 30% platform automation and 70% full-stack feature development.
What You’ll Be Doing
Accelerate SOC 2 compliance. Work with leadership to implement, automate, and maintain the AWS security controls SOC 2 requires: encryption at rest and in transit, least-privilege IAM, logging, and vulnerability scanning.
Build our ITAR environment. Help design and run an isolated AWS GovCloud environment for customers with export-controlled data, with access restricted to US persons.
Own the platform. Manage, monitor, and scale our AWS environment using infrastructure as code (Terraform, AWS CDK, or Pulumi), with no manual configuration drift.
Build across the stack. Design, write, and deploy maintainable backend APIs and frontend features for our core product.
Automate everything. Maintain CI/CD pipelines (such as GitHub Actions) with automated testing, dependency scanning, and secure deployments built in.
Keep the architecture lean. Favor managed AWS services so the infrastructure needs minimal babysitting and you can focus on product.
Experience
A hybrid mindset. You’re a product-minded developer who moved toward DevOps because you wanted your code to ship faster, safer, and more securely.
AWS expertise. Deep hands-on experience with managed and serverless AWS services, such as Elastic Beanstalk, Lambda, RDS, SQS, Cognito, IAM, and CloudTrail.
Infrastructure as code. Proven experience managing cloud environments entirely through code (such as Terraform or AWS CDK) rather than the console.
Security and compliance experience. You’ve configured cloud environments to pass frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA. Experience with Vanta, Drata, or Secureframe is a big plus.
Full-stack proficiency. Strong production experience with Node.js and TypeScript, React, and PostgreSQL.
Startup agility. You’ve been an early engineer or on a lean team where you owned your deployments and wore multiple hats.
Nice to Have
Experience with queue-based background processing (SQS), PDF and CAD file processing, or LLM-backed features in production.
Experience with AWS GovCloud, FedRAMP, NIST 800-171, or CMMC.
Experience supporting customers with ITAR or other export-controlled data.
A passion for CAD, hardware, or manufacturing.

description:

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

We are seeking a Sr. Cost Accountant to join our diverse and discerning finance and accounting team!  Specifically, we are looking for someone who is ready for growth in their career and ready to tackle challenges as the company grows and changes.  Reporting to the Assistant Controller, this role will have extensive opportunities to improve processes and controls; as well as drive efficiencies throughout the cost accounting processes in our flagship, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility.  Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Standard costing and cost accounting
   
   - Develop, maintain, and update standard costs, BOM/routing roll-ups, and labor and overhead rates
   
   - Record and reconcile material, labor, and overhead costs to the general ledger
   
   Work order and variance analysis
   
   - Analyze work orders for cost overruns, yield/scrap, and efficiency issues
   
   - Calculate and explain purchase price, material usage, labor, overhead, and yield variances; identify root causes in partnering with FP&A and Operations.
   
   Inventory and WIP accounting
   
   - Own inventory valuation, roll-forward, and COGS reconciliations
   
   - Evaluate excess and obsolete (E&O) and lower-of-cost-or-NRV reserves
   
   - Collaborate with Warehousing team in their execution of cycle and physical counts, including validation that adjustments made were approved as per the Company’s approval process
   
   Close, reporting, and audit
   
   - Prepare cost-related journal entries, reconciliations, and flux analysis for month-end close
   
   - Support budgeting, forecasting, and product/project profitability analysis
   
   - Provide documentation and support for internal and external audits
   
   Controls and process improvement
   
   - Design, document, and test inventory and cost controls (SOX where applicable)
   
   - Identify opportunities to automate recurring reconciliations, reporting, and variance workflows




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - CPA licensed

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting

 - 3–5 years of progressive US GAAP accounting experience (at least 2 years in public accounting)

 - Experience in a start-up, high-growth, or first-of-a-kind manufacturing environment a plus

 - Hands-on experience with standard costing, BOM/routing cost roll-ups, and inventory valuation

 - Experience with ERP systems (Oracle Fusion a plus) and using AI tools

This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. Relocation assistance is available.

title: Head of Sales
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the role
As Head of Sales, you'll own Formic's sales strategy, execution, team performance, and revenue generation results. Your responsibility is to grow and manage a high-performing sales organization that consistently wins new business while concurrently growing and expanding within existing customers.
We're looking for a commercially astute builder who knows how to turn complex customer needs into successful sales. You'll develop a sharp understanding of manufacturers, their operational challenges, and the economics of automation, then use customer insights and performance data to strengthen targeting, sales execution, and growth. You'll be responsible for helping to identify what is working, change what isn’t, and implement effective practices to drive sales success.
You'll lead and develop our Sales team, identifying what makes our best customer engagements and salespeople successful and turning those insights into better coaching, stronger qualification, higher conversion, and more consistent performance. You’ll leverage data and insights derived from Formic’s range of GTM tools and tech stack, customer feedback, and feedback from other Formic teams (i.e Customer Success, Solutions, Service, etc.) to continuously improve the sales process and methodologies to better align with unmet customer need and desired outcomes.  You'll stay close to important deals and help the team navigate operational, financial, and technical stakeholders with confidence.
This is a hands-on leadership role requiring a combination of strategic judgment, direct & active team management, and tactical execution. You'll challenge assumptions, make decisions grounded in data and customer insights, prototype, test, iterate, and ultimately implement changes, and measure their impact quantitatively and qualitatively. Working across the business, you'll build a more effective, predictable, and scalable sales organization.
What You'll Do
Sales strategy and execution
Own sales targets, territory strategy, account prioritization, and revenue performance. Establish clear standards for opportunity ownership, workload distribution, response times, pipeline progression, and follow-through; proactively resolve stalled opportunities, capacity constraints, and performance gaps.
Study target producers and manufacturers, applications, buying processes, and competitive alternatives to focus effort on the best opportunities.
Improve discovery, qualification, business cases, proposals, negotiations, and closing; participate directly in high-stakes deals.
Personally own and drive select sales opportunities each quarter to maintain firsthand knowledge of our customers, product, and sales process.
Establish rapid iteration and testing of new or modified sales approaches and tactics, accounting for differences in regions, markets, and application verticals
Balance customer value, pricing, profitability, technical feasibility, and deployment requirements when evaluating opportunities.
Sales leadership and coaching
Build and lead a disciplined sales management organization. Recruit, develop, and hold accountable sellers and managers; equip regional leads with clear expectations, performance metrics, coaching practices, and the skills to develop their teams while maintaining their own commercial effectiveness.
Use call observation, deal reviews, customer feedback, and performance data to understand why individuals and deals succeed or stall.
Translate top-performer practices into repeatable training, targeted coaching, and stronger team-wide performance.
Validate impacts and results of training, coaching, and enablement to ensure the team’s performance is quantitatively improving as a result.
Sales operations and collaboration
Build reliable forecasting, CRM discipline, meaningful metrics, and operating routines that surface opportunities and risks early.
Improve sales processes, tools, reporting, and resource allocation; test changes and measure their impact.
Establish a disciplined operating partnership with Marketing and Sales Development, jointly refining the ideal customer profile, account priorities, qualification standards, opportunity handoffs, sales follow-through, and feedback from won and lost deals to improve pipeline quality and conversion.
Coordinate with Solutions, Engineering, Operations, and Customer Success on feasibility, customer commitments, and handoffs. Own commercial execution for expansion within existing accounts, partnering with Customer Success to surface whitespace, prioritize opportunities, and ensure accountable follow-through.
What makes you a great fit
Curiosity and a demonstrated desire to learn and serve customers
Demonstrated success building sales capabilities, operating rhythms, and team performance in a growing B2B business, including driving process change and improvements while ensuring existing momentum is maintained
Exceptional coach who diagnoses performance gaps and helps people improve through direct feedback and practical training.
Experience leading consultative sales of complex technical or operational solutions, navigating plant-level stakeholders, financial decision-makers, implementation considerations, and extended sales cycles.
Strong analytical and commercial judgment, including pipeline analysis, forecasting, deal economics, and Salesforce or similar CRM tools.
Hands-on, resourceful leader who can build processes, recruit talent, make difficult decisions, and close important deals.
Experience selling hardware or equipment into manufacturing operations is a plus.
What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.
Equal Opportunity Employment:
Formic is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to accessibility@formic.co .
AI Use:
At Formic, fairness and transparency are at the heart of our hiring process. We use AI-powered tools in some interviews to help our teams evaluate candidate responses, but all final hiring decisions are made by humans. You can learn more about how AI is used in our recruitment process by reviewing our AI Hiring Disclosure linked  here .

Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.

description:
