If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The Advanced Product Development (APD) team leverages and advances the cutting-edge of technology to design and develop the surgical robotic systems of the future. Robotics Algorithms and Controls engineers (Systems Analysts) perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the da Vinci product line. They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to challenging problems.
As a Senior Systems Analyst you will work with a small, multidisciplinary team of talented and dedicated engineers. This position is the software-oriented track within Systems Analysis, bridging the team’s algorithms and the software infrastructure they run on. You will own the software layer between the application and the real-time control loop, the bring-up of the embedded compute platform, the software side of the FPGA interface, and you will bring enough fluency in control algorithms to connect their signals to the right system modes and safety responses. Systems Analysts maintain awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to medical devices and safety-critical systems and actively apply this knowledge to system design.
Essential Job Duties
•       Design, implement, and own the software layer between the application software and the real-time control loop.
•       Bring up the embedded compute platform and real-time execution environment for new prototype systems.
•       Own the software interface to the FPGA, including drivers and data paths between processors and FPGA logic.
•       Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems and lead embedded bring-up of new manipulators, instruments, and controller boards.
•       Implement control and safety algorithms developed with Systems Analysts as deterministic, production-quality embedded software.
•       Design and implement servo control systems with Systems Analysts, applying control theory to mechatronic and tele-robotic platforms.
•       Connect algorithm signals to the appropriate system modes and safety responses in partnership with the Systems Analysts who own the supervisory logic.
•       Root-cause problems that cross the hardware, software, and control boundary.
•       Develop test, continuous integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop infrastructure for Systems Analysis software; provide tool building for other engineering issues.
•       Document software design, risks, requirements, and test protocols; document and communicate intellectual property.
•       Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
•       Communicate system performance to the organization and support it as products evolve from design engineering to manufacturing.
•       Act as an interface between Systems Analysis and Software Engineering; take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries.
Required Skills and Experience
•       Strong embedded development skills, including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++, and experience with unit testing, continuous integration, and modern build systems.
•       Experience developing software under real-time constraints, with a solid understanding of determinism, latency, and execution-time analysis.
•       Experience with embedded architectures on multi-processor SoC/FPGA platforms, including bare-metal or RTOS development, device drivers, and inter-processor communication.
•       Hands-on experience bringing up embedded platforms and integrating prototype hardware with software.
•       Working knowledge of control systems and robotics sufficient to read, modify, and reason about control code and its timing.
•       MATLAB and Python programming capabilities for analysis, simulation, and tool building.
•       Comfort with the concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
•       Detail-oriented, with the ability to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
•       Hands-on engineering experience with a proven ability to work well in a team environment.
•       Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.
•       A desire to deliver a quality and innovative product that will improve millions of people’s lives.
Required Education and Training
•       Minimum MS degree in CS, EE, ME, or a similar field with 4–5+ years of industrial experience, or a PhD with 1–3+ years of experience, or a BS with 7+ years of relevant industrial experience.
Working Conditions
•       Position is primarily office/lab-based (Sunnyvale, CA). Requires regular access to prototype and lab environments with standard safety precautions. Up to 10% travel for clinical site visits, partner meetings, or conference participation.
Preferred Skills and Experience
•       Experience designing and implementing servo control systems, or a deeper robotics and controls background.
•       Medical device or safety-critical system product experience (FDA design controls, ISO 13485, ISO 14971).
•       Experience with surgical robotics, haptics, or tele-presence system design.
•       Familiarity with FPGA-based motor control or other embedded real-time architectures.
•       Experience developing products in a highly regulated environment, including through FDA clearance.

Lead Supplier Engineer on a design project. Demonstrable expertise across a wide range of manufacturing processes, with deep specialization in metal fabrication including Precision machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding processes, surface treatment and coatings, Clear understanding of key input variables impacting quality, cost, cycle time and capacity.

Strong Project Management skills, with ability to manage multiple suppliers, timelines, and cross functional dependencies.

Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with sound engineering judgement and data-driven decision making.
Proficiency in ERP/MRP systems (preferably SAP) and strong working knowledge of MS office tools.
Ability to read, interpret, and communicate complex mechanical drawings and specifications
Required Education and Training
Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mechanical, Manufacturing, or related field)
8+ years of relevant experience in Supplier Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or Mechanical Design or related field.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with GD&T, tolerance stack-up analysis, and metrology techniques
Knowledge of cutting-edge technologies used in metal fabrication in machining and sheet metal assembly, apply the supplier’s process capability to provide the design solutions.
Familiarity with electro-mechanical assemblies and CAD tools
Experience in regulated environments (ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820)
Background in Lean, Six Sigma, or SPC implementation
Experience with supplier audits, process validation, and qualification

Primary Function of Position:
As a  Staff Product Security Engineer , you will be the guardian of our next-generation platforms, including the  da Vinci 4 (dV4),  the groundbreaking  da Vinci 5 (dV5)  and backend infrastructure.
This isn't just a "cloud security" job—it’s a multifaceted role requiring you to secure hardware in the field, build intelligent threat detection for global medical infrastructure, and lead Incident Response (IR) when every second counts.
We are looking for a security pioneer who leverages  AI and Machine Learning  to automate defense and identify anomalies that traditional rule-based systems miss.
Essential Job Duties:
• Platform Security (dV4 & dV5): Lead security architecture reviews and threat modeling for robotic systems deployed globally. Ensure the integrity of embedded systems and real-time telemetry.
• Infrastructure Threat Detection: Design and deploy advanced monitoring solutions across our connected surgical ecosystem. You will bridge the gap between traditional IT security and specialized OT (Operational Technology) security.
• AI/ML-Driven Defense: Develop and implement ML models to detect anomalous behavior in robot telemetry, network traffic, and system logs to preemptively identify potential exploits or hardware tampering.
• Incident Response & Digital Forensics: Lead IR functions for product-related security events. This includes developing playbooks specifically tailored for robotic surgical environments and coordinating with cross-functional engineering teams.
• Vulnerability Research: Conduct deep-dive analysis into emerging threats targeting IoT and medical devices, ensuring Intuitive stays ahead of the curve.
Skills, Experience, Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/ Engineering/ Information Security / Cybersecurity
8+ years of security engineering or product security experience (or equivalent).
Strong understanding of device/embedded security, cloud security (AWS/Azure/GCP), and hybrid architectures.
Experience with security monitoring, log pipelines, and SIEM/SOAR tools.
Hands-on expertise with automation frameworks (Python, Go, scripting) and cloud-native tooling.
Familiarity with AI/ML concepts as applied to detection engineering and anomaly analysis.
Hands-on experience leading or contributing to security incident response for production systems.
Ability to triage complex events involving firmware, cloud services, device telemetry, user behavior, or third-party dependencies.
Experience generating incident timelines, technical RCA documentation, and corrective action plans.
Strong understanding of digital forensics concepts, memory/log analysis, and evidence integrity for regulated systems.
Deep knowledge of:
Vulnerability classes and secure coding patterns
Encryption, key management, certificates
Network and protocol security
API and microservices security
Container and orchestration security

title: Controls Technician
description:
Job Description:
Mars Snacking - Controls Technician - TNN
Area: 3
Hiring Manager: Scott Walther
Shift Schedule: Rotating night shift 2-2-3
Hours: 6:45 AM - 7:15 PM (Must be flexible pending business needs).
The Controls Technician will maintain, adjust, troubleshoot and repair electrical equipment such as motors, motor control circuits, power distribution systems up to 480 VAC, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC's focusing on Rockwell and Siemens) and AC/DC drives. The incumbent must be capable of using electrical test equipment, meters, o-scopes, etc., and possess the skills required to troubleshoot to a component level.  Additional requirements include knowledge of robotics, automated processes, and photoelectric and ultrasonic sensors.  The incumbent must also be able to read wiring diagrams and schematics and understand the software associated with PLC's in order to troubleshoot issues.  In addition, the incumbent assists the Maintenance Mechanics when troubleshooting issues.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Qualifications :
Obtain line manager approval.
Meet the required time-in-role criteria
Maintain good standing status (See definition below).
High school diploma and minimum of three to five years' experience in a TPM/technical, manufacturing environment.
Preferred Qualifications :
A technical degree in Industrial Maintenance, Electrical/Controls or related engineering/technical fields.
Physical Requirements :
Perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.
Frequent lifting/carrying (10–50 lbs) and pushing/pulling (50–300 lbs).
Frequent bending, stooping, twisting, handling, and gripping.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Responsible for the maintenance and troubleshooting of electrical and control systems equipment down to the component level, including 480V electrical power distribution, instrumentation, motor controls, VFD’s, Servo’s, I/O devices/modules, PLC’s, HMI’s, and control networks.
Troubleshoot machine breakdowns and malfunctions utilizing a working knowledge of control system programs and tools required to troubleshoot PLC’s, HMI’s, and VFD/servo systems including electrical schematics, programming software, meters, and other electrical test equipment.
Repair, replace and calibrate all electrical sensing devices, instrumentation including photoelectric, inductive, capacitive, pressure, temperature, weight, position sensors, flow, and analytical instruments.
Coordinate the electrical preventative maintenance program by identifying items that need regular inspection and replacement, scheduling the tasks and task frequencies required, and following up to ensure the completion and effectiveness of each task.
Manage all PLC, Servo and HMI programs and changes as well as electrical documentation.  Ensure that they are all accurate, updated, and available to the technicians and archived at regular intervals.
Other job duties as assigned by your Line Manager.

The opportunity to learn and develop, taking charge of your own career across Mars.
An industry-competitive salary and great benefits package.
The chance to work cross-functionally and add value and impact to the business.
If you are passionate, a great problem solver, resilient, and have a high drive for results, then we want to hear from you!

description:
Overview
Microsoft Customer and Partner Solutions-Core (MCAPS) accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. By uniting product, engineering, marketing, sales, customer success, and partners around a common customer mission, we help customers realize value faster and turn innovation into measurable business impact. Through deep technical expertise and differentiated go-to-market execution, we win competitively, capture market share, and scale repeatable growth motions. We differentiate through value creation - delivering world-class, AI-powered customer experiences that accelerate adoption, strengthen loyalty, and create sustainable competitive advantage, driving growth that outpaces the market.
The Strategy & Transformation team identifies emerging opportunities and drives programmatic transformation across MCAPS Core, our customers, partners, and account teams. We design and test new programs, operating models, and customer experiences, then we scale what works to deliver AI-first transformation, customer growth, and measurable commercial impact.
The Principal Partner Ecosystem Strategy Lead is a senior strategy role responsible for identifying and advancing high-impact growth opportunities across Microsoft's partner and ISV ecosystem.
The role operates across complex organizational, commercial, technical, and go-to-market boundaries where the opportunity is often emerging, ownership is distributed, and the path forward is not yet defined.
This leader will independently interpret signals from partners, customers, field teams, business performance, and market dynamics to identify systemic barriers or untapped opportunities that could materially affect partner-led growth. They will determine which opportunities warrant investment, develop the strategic hypothesis and business case, and work across Microsoft organizations to validate the opportunity through analysis, customer and partner evidence, and focused pilots.
For opportunities that prove material, this leader will establish the strategy and intervention, mobilize the right cross-functional teams to test it, define measures of success, and ultimately transition proven motions or mechanisms to the appropriate long-term business owner.
This is not a traditional partner management or program management role. It requires strategic judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to create clarity and momentum across complex problems without relying on formal authority or established playbooks.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Identify and Prioritize Growth Opportunities
Interpret partner, customer, field, market, and business signals to identify systemic barriers and emerging opportunities for partner-led growth.
Connect signals across commercial models, incentives, customer engagement, technical investment, Marketplace, field execution, and partner strategy to identify opportunities that may not be visible within any single organization.
Distinguish between isolated operational friction and systemic constraints that materially affect growth.
Develop clear hypotheses about the business opportunity, affected behavior, potential intervention, and expected impact.
Make disciplined recommendations about which opportunities to advance, which belong with existing business owners, and which should not consume additional investment.
Validate and Incubate Strategic Opportunities
Lead discovery and validation of ambiguous, cross-organizational opportunities before significant investment is made.
Develop the evidence, business case, success measures, and decision criteria required to determine whether an opportunity should advance.
Partner with product management and other business, technical, commercial, and field teams across Microsoft to design focused pilots and experiments.
Establish clear go/no-go criteria and use evidence to refine, scale, redirect, or stop initiatives.
Maintain strategic ownership of the opportunity while drawing on functional experts and execution teams across Microsoft.
Design Scalable Growth Mechanisms
Translate validated opportunities into repeatable growth motions, operating mechanisms, commercial approaches, or changes to existing business processes.
Identify where organizational seams, incentives, ownership models, or existing mechanisms inhibit partner-led growth and determine the highest-leverage intervention.
Define how successful interventions can operate through existing Microsoft organizations rather than creating unnecessary parallel structures.
Develop clear ownership, measurement, governance, and transition models for initiatives that prove successful.
Influence and Mobilize Across Microsoft
Build coalitions across business groups, sales, engineering, commercial, finance, Marketplace, partner, and customer organizations.
Navigate situations in which multiple organizations own portions of a problem but no organization owns the end-to-end opportunity.
Influence senior stakeholders through evidence, strategic clarity, and business impact rather than positional authority.
Establish enough alignment to move from an ambiguous opportunity to a bounded test and ultimately to an organizational decision.
Scale and Transition
Define what must be true before an incubated initiative is ready to scale.
Establish measurable evidence that an intervention changes partner, customer, seller, or business outcomes.
Identify the appropriate long-term business owner and build the mechanisms required for a successful transition.
Ensure successful work becomes embedded into durable business processes rather than remaining dependent on the strategy team.

Can move fluidly between strategy, business models, commercial considerations, customer scenarios, technology, and organizational design.
Understands partner and ISV business models and how partners create customer and platform value.
Can engage credibly with product, engineering, sales, finance, commercial, partner, and executive stakeholders.
Knows how to find the real business constraint beneath a collection of symptoms.
Can design a lightweight test or pilot rather than defaulting immediately to a large program.
Is comfortable driving work through people and organizations they do not manage.
Can challenge assumptions while building the coalition necessary to move an idea forward.
Measures success through business impact and behavior change, not activity.

Can build something important and then deliberately hand it to someone else to run.

Failure-driven self-improvement:  improve long-horizon agents by diagnosing failure modes in their trajectories and synthesizing targeted post-training data that closes specific capability gaps.

title: Senior Security Operations Engineer
description:
Overview
Team overview
Every cloud depends on a small set of foundational services that almost everything else trusts. Together they form the cloud's Trusted Computing Base (TCB): the services where a small gap can have an outsized blast radius across the cloud and the customers who depend on it.
These are Microsoft's crown jewels, and protecting them is urgent: sophisticated attackers target exactly these kinds of services, and AI is making it faster to find and exploit weaknesses. Securing them is always top of mind for senior leadership, it comes first when we prioritize risk reduction, and the controls we prove here set the paved path for production services across the company.
The TCB Core Security Engineering team in IAM Protect, part of Microsoft's CISO organization, leads this work. We take a data-driven, attack-path view of risk, modeling the trust relationships between services to understand blast radius and focus our effort where it reduces the most risk. We are a technically deep security that operates horizontally across Microsoft. Our strategy is simple to state and hard to do: isolate these services from the rest of the cloud, minimize what has to be trusted, and defend what remains with layered controls.
Role overview
We are looking for a Senior Security Operations Engineer who pairs a deep understanding of how cloud services and platforms are actually constructed with the security instincts to see where they can be broken. You will identify new risks to our crown jewel services, model them with our attack-path and risk data, develop the policies and security controls that close them, and partner with leaders and service owners across Microsoft to drive those controls to adoption until the exposure is measurably gone. Every attack path you shut down is one no attacker can use against Microsoft's cloud or its customers.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
Responsibilities
•    Identify and analyze risk across our most critical cloud services. Look for unintended trust and access paths into them, such as excessive privilege, credential exposure and unnecessary access between services, and turn findings into clear, prioritized risk statements.
•    Model risk with data. Work with service owners and architects to understand how their services are built, represent trust relationships accurately, and use attack-path analysis to quantify blast radius and decide which paths to remove first.
•    Develop security policies and controls that are enforceable by default rather than dependent on reviews, such as isolation boundaries, least privilege and hardening standards, each with a clear scope, safe rollout, exception handling and validation telemetry.
•    Drive risk burn-down to closure. Lead campaigns with service owners and engineering leaders across Microsoft, set targets, track progress with data, unblock teams, manage exceptions with discipline and report measurable risk reduction to senior leadership.
•    Leverage AI to automate workflows, improve efficiency, and streamline your work.
•    Govern and defend the boundary around these services. Define and run the mechanisms that keep the set of critical services small and well isolated, and partner with detection, incident response and eviction teams so we can assume breach and still contain an attacker quickly.
•    Turn incidents and red team findings into durable protection by converting the lessons into risk models, policies and controls, so the same path cannot be used twice.
•    Scale your impact with data and automation: build KQL queries, datasets, dashboards and AI-assisted tooling that make risk discovery, prioritization and campaign tracking faster.
•    Produce crisp technical artifacts, including risk write-ups, control specifications, troubleshooting guides and leadership updates that unblock execution.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 4+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR equivalent experience. Other requirements: ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements is required for this role. These include, but are not limited to, the Microsoft Cloud Background Check: this position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire or transfer and every two years thereafter.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 6+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 8+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection
OR equivalent experience.
•    6+ years of experience in cloud security engineering, security architecture, offensive security or incident response in a hyperscale or large enterprise environment.
•    Deep knowledge of how cloud services are constructed: identity and token issuance (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and service-to-service authentication), service principals and managed identities, PKI and certificate lifecycle, secret and key management, role-based access and control-plane authorization, build and release pipelines, and network segmentation.
•    Experience with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft's production environments, including Secure Future Initiative work, or equivalent experience at another cloud provider.
•    Experience modeling attack paths and blast radius with attack graphs or graph analytics (for example, BloodHound-style analysis) and using them to prioritize mitigations.
•    A proven record of designing enforceable security policies or guardrails and driving their adoption across many engineering teams to measurable risk reduction.
•    Fluency in KQL (Azure Data Explorer/Kusto) or similar query languages, plus scripting in Python or PowerShell to analyze large datasets and automate.
•    Working knowledge of attacker tradecraft (MITRE ATT&CK, privilege escalation, lateral movement and persistence) from red team, penetration testing or incident response work.
•    The ability to influence senior engineering leaders and service owners without direct authority, with clear and concise writing.
•    Industry certifications such as CISSP CISA CISM SANS OSCP Security+

Microsoft is a company where passionate innovators come to collaborate, envision what can be and take their careers further. This is a world of more possibilities, more innovation, more openness, and the sky is the limit thinking in a cloud-enabled world.
Microsoft’s Azure Data engineering team is leading the transformation of analytics in the world of data with products like databases, data integration, big data analytics, messaging & real-time analytics, and business intelligence. The products our portfolio include Microsoft Fabric, Azure SQL DB, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure PostgreSQL, Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure Service Bus, Azure Event Grid, and Power BI. Our mission is to build the data platform for the age of AI, powering a new class of data-first applications and driving a data culture.

Our portfolio includes SQL, Azure Cosmos DB, DocumentDB, PostgreSQL, and MySQL, supporting developers as they build AI native applications and run critical workloads at global scale.​

The Gateway sits on the request path between customers and Azure Cosmos DB, processing trillions of requests every day across hundreds of clusters worldwide. Our team owns the scalability, availability, performance, and operational excellence of this infrastructure and is building the next generation of the Cosmos DB Gateway to significantly increase throughput, reduce latency, improve resiliency, and lower infrastructure cost.
We do not just value differences or different perspectives. We seek them out and invite them in so we can tap into the collective power of everyone in the company. As a result, our customers are better served.

Dive deep into Azure technologies and distributed database systems.
Collaborate with partners, internal and external to Azure Cosmos DB organization, to design and build features that drive service growth.

Work in a culture of continuous improvement, adaptation, reflection, and growth.

title: Site Logistics Engineer
description:
Overview
The Logistics Coordinator supports the safe, efficient, and on-time delivery of data center construction projects by assisting with site logistics planning, coordination, and execution. This role contributes to ensuring that materials, equipment, workforce movement, and site access are organized and aligned with project schedules and safety standards.
Working closely with Construction Managers, Project Managers, contractors, and cross-functional stakeholders, this role provides hands-on support for day-to-day site logistics activities, tracking progress, and helping to identify and communicate coordination issues impacting delivery.
Success in this role requires strong organization, attention to detail, a willingness to learn, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced construction environment. Ideal candidates are early-career professionals with a background in construction, engineering, architecture, or a related discipline who are eager to build foundational project delivery capabilities within Microsoft’s Data Center Development (DCD) organization.
This position is based in South Bend, Indiana.
Relocation assistance will be provided. Candidates selected for this role are expected to relocate and live within 50 miles of the designated work location
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment where every employee can contribute, grow, and make an impact
Responsibilities
Site Logistics Support
Support coordination of site logistics activities including material deliveries, equipment staging, workforce access, and traffic flow
Assist in maintaining site logistics plans, laydown areas, and access routes in alignment with site requirements
Coordinate with contractors and vendors to support alignment of delivery activities with site readiness and construction sequencing
Support development and enhancement of project coordination tools and workflows using Microsoft Copilot and digital platforms

Safety, Security & Site Compliance
Support a safety- and security-first culture by promoting awareness of site safety policies, physical security requirements, and access protocols
Observe and communicate potential safety or security concerns (e.g., site access, badging, restricted areas) to appropriate stakeholders
Participate in site walkthroughs and observe logistics-related risks (e.g., congestion areas, delivery conflicts, access routes)
Communicate observations and escalate concerns to appropriate project stakeholders

Communicate and coordinate with general contractors, subcontractors, and internal Microsoft teams to support day-to-day logistics activities
Assist in identifying and communicating logistics issues or conflicts to appropriate stakeholders to support timely resolution
Support alignment of logistics plans with field conditions and contractor execution activities
Assist in tracking contractor deliverables and coordination items
Assist in tracking project issues, changes, and coordination impacts to support team visibility and alignment
Support quality and field verification efforts by assisting with tracking of inspections, observations, and completion of work in alignment with project requirements

Maintain project SharePoint sites and document repositories to support consistent organization, accessibility, and alignment with team standards
Assist in ensuring project documentation is up to date, properly stored, and accessible to stakeholders
Assist DCD Construction Managers and Directors in preparing presentations, reporting materials, and meeting documentation (e.g., slide decks, meeting minutes, coordination updates)
Support collection and organization of project data to develop reporting visuals, progress summaries, and basic metrics tracking

As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. title: Software Engineer, Agent Identity
description:
About the Team

The Agent Identity team builds the foundational identity infrastructure that enables AI agents to securely act on behalf of users and organizations. We develop the systems that allow agents to establish their identity, demonstrate whose authority they are operating under, and securely access resources across applications and environments.

Our team owns agent identity and delegation, authentication and authorization, credential lifecycle management, revocation, and integrations with external platforms. We also build Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling OpenAI to serve as an identity provider across a growing ecosystem of applications.

As AI agents become increasingly autonomous, our work is foundational to how users, organizations, and developers establish trust in agentic systems.

About the Role

We are looking for experienced software engineers to design and build the identity infrastructure powering the next generation of AI agents across OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and Codex.

You will tackle complex, largely unsolved engineering challenges at the intersection of identity, security, distributed systems, and agent infrastructure. You’ll help define how agents authenticate across environments, how users securely delegate authority to agents, and how agents interact with external applications and services.

This is an opportunity to shape foundational technical primitives at OpenAI while helping influence how the broader industry approaches identity in an increasingly agent-driven world.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and build foundational agent identity primitives, including agent authentication, delegated authorization, and credential lifecycle management.

 - Develop secure mechanisms that enable agents to act on behalf of users and organizations across internal and external systems.

 - Architect authentication and authorization flows for connectors, third-party applications, and cloud-based agent execution environments.

 - Build and evolve Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling secure identity federation and interoperability across the broader application ecosystem.

 - Design highly scalable, reliable, and secure distributed systems that support credential issuance, rotation, revocation, and access enforcement.

 - Partner closely with engineering, product, security, and external platform teams to solve emerging identity challenges and help shape industry standards.

 - Drive technical direction and own complex initiatives from initial architecture through production deployment.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or business-critical backend infrastructure.

 - Have deep technical experience in identity and access management, workload identity, identity providers, authentication, authorization, or credential lifecycle management.

 - Alternatively, have experience building cloud-based AI agents, agent execution environments, browser-based automation, or connector infrastructure, with firsthand exposure to identity and authentication challenges.

 - Have familiarity with identity and authorization protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, or related emerging standards.

 - Bring a security-first mindset and proactively consider trust boundaries, failure modes, and potential abuse when designing systems.

 - Thrive in ambiguous problem spaces where established technical patterns may not yet exist, and enjoy defining solutions from first principles.

 - Have a track record of driving complex technical initiatives, influencing architectural decisions, and collaborating effectively across engineering teams.

 - Are excited about defining how identity, trust, and delegated authority will work in a world where AI agents increasingly act on our behalf.

OpenAI's Governance, Risk, and Compliance team works within Security to connect obligations and customer commitments to effective controls and reliable evidence. We partner across the organization to make security easier to put into practice and easier to understand.

You will discover what users need, decide what to build and sequence first, and personally implement data models, integrations, and working workflows. You will carry those products through testing, adoption, and operation.

You may spend one part of the day debugging a data flow and another explaining the architecture, evidence, and tradeoffs to leadership or an external audience. In this role, you will:

 - Own the product vision and technical direction for an agreed portfolio of GRC systems, discovering user needs and deciding what to build and sequence first.

 - Design and build scalable data models, integrations, and workflows that connect requirements, systems, people, controls, actions, and evidence.

 - Establish data quality, ownership, history, and freshness practices so changes and missing information produce accurate, useful behavior.

Collaboration & Developer Support Engineering Partnership: Act as a strategic partner to development teams, identifying pipeline bottlenecks and providing actionable solutions for build and release challenges. Technical Mentorship: Provide expert guidance on CI/CD best practices, release engineering strategies, and GitOps deployments. Experience: 7–10 years in Platform Engineering, Developer Experience, Build and Release Engineering, or DevOps, supporting large-scale software engineering organizations. DevEx Focus: Proven track record of improving developer productivity, building self-service platforms, and reducing friction in the software development lifecycle. CI/CD & Release Expertise: Proven track record of building complex, automated CI/CD pipelines and leading release management processes. Deep familiarity with enterprise CI/CD platforms and container registries. Continuous Improvement
Best Practices: Maintain best practices and utilize data management tools for enhanced efficiency.

Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with experience working closely with leadership or sales teams.

In this role, you will:
Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.
Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.
Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.
Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.

Samsara ships fast, and we're looking for a Communications Manager to make sure the market understands what we've built and why it matters. This is a high-impact, high-autonomy role for someone who knows how to build media relationships, narratives, and programs, and who can move quickly in a complex, fast-changing environment.
You'll lead communications for Samsara's partnerships and support product communications. You'll shape how Samsara shows up in the market: in top-tier business and technology press, alongside our partners' announcements, and through the relationships you build with reporters. You'll work closely with the broader communications team and partner with Product, Product Marketing, and Partner Marketing.
If you're a hungry, technically savvy go-getter who thrives without a lot of hand-holding, builds real relationships with business and tech media, and actively uses AI and agentic workflows to move faster, scale your output, and elevate your craft, we want to talk to you.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in New York or San Francisco, with in-person time as needed.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.

Lead partnership communications
Lead communications for Samsara's partnerships, including technology and connectivity, insurance, OEM and ecosystem partners
Work directly with partners' communications teams to align on the narrative, proof points, timing and who drives the announcement
Draft press releases, joint announcements, quotes and press materials, and pitch them to the media
Elevate high-profile partnerships into stories that strengthen Samsara's position in the market, while efficiently handling more routine announcements
Build a repeatable partnership go-to-market communications plan that the team can reuse
Partner with partner marketing, product and other teams across several parts of the business
Support product communications
Support the head of product communications on announcements and pitching, using product and product marketing messaging and proof points to shape how each launch lands in the press
lead smaller launches, with the opportunity to take on more over time
Turn technical product features into clear, compelling stories
Build media relationships
Build trusted relationships with top-tier business and technology reporters
Understand what reporters are covering and find the right angles for Samsara
Become a go-to source for the media on Samsara news
Work across the business
Collaborate with Product, Product Marketing, Partner Marketing, Content Marketing and Creative
Support the team on other external communications as priorities shift
Use AI in your day-to-day work
Minimum requirements
5+ years of experience in communications or public relations, with a background in B2B or technology companies (startup experience preferred).

Experience in product and/or partnerships communications, even if it was not your sole focus
Strong technical fluency, with the ability to understand and clearly explain complex products

Excellent writing skills
Existing relationships with reporters, or a clear ability and willingness to build them by meeting people one-on-one
A self-starter who figures things out independently and does not back away from a problem
Comfortable aligning stakeholders across companies and teams
An ideal candidate also has
A degree in journalism or a writing-focused field
Experience writing and launching partnership announcements, including with large brand partners
Experience with hardware, IoT, AI or industrial technology
Experience at a fast-growing or publicly traded B2B technology company
Interest in learning data-driven storytelling

Define the Future of Data Engineering
Develop multi-year technical roadmaps for enterprise data engineering capabilities, platforms, and data products.
Establish target-state architectures for ingestion, transformation, orchestration, storage, serving, and consumption of enterprise data.
Define engineering strategies that support both analytical and operational workloads while enabling AI and intelligent experiences.
Drive modernization from tightly coupled pipelines and point solutions toward reusable, scalable, metadata-driven data platforms.

Establish patterns that allow data to be consumed consistently by analytics, applications, APIs, AI systems, and enterprise platforms.

Establish data-product engineering practices that treat enterprise datasets as discoverable, governed, reliable, and reusable products.
Define standards for data contracts, ownership, service-level objectives, quality, lineage, documentation, and discoverability.
Drive engineering approaches that make trusted enterprise data available through tables, APIs, events, semantic layers, and AI-accessible interfaces.
Drive Engineering Excellence
Establish engineering standards for design, development, testing, deployment, observability, and production support.
Define patterns for automated testing across data pipelines, including unit, integration, data-quality, regression, and contract testing.
Drive observability practices across pipelines and data products, including freshness, completeness, quality, latency, failure detection, and cost.
Influence and Mentor
Serve as a trusted technical advisor to engineering, product, data, analytics, and technology leaders.
Provide technical leadership across teams without relying on direct organizational authority.
Mentor senior engineers, lead engineers, and engineering managers on architecture and engineering practices.
Create reference implementations, reusable components, engineering standards, and technical documentation that accelerate other teams.
Lead design reviews and technical communities of practice.
Raise engineering standards through code reviews, architecture reviews, technical deep dives, and hands-on problem solving.
Foster a culture of engineering excellence, experimentation, accountability, operational ownership, and continuous learning.
We'd love to hear from people with...
Required Qualifications
12+ years of software, data, or platform engineering experience.
8+ years designing and building large-scale data platforms, pipelines, or distributed data systems.
Demonstrated experience serving as a technical lead for complex, enterprise-scale engineering initiatives.
Deep expertise in modern data engineering concepts including distributed processing, data modeling, orchestration, data quality, metadata, lineage, and data lifecycle management.
Strong hands-on experience with SQL and at least one general-purpose programming language such as Python, Java, or Scala.
Experience designing highly available, scalable, secure, observable, and cost-efficient production data platforms.
Strong understanding of DevOps and DataOps practices including CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, automated testing, monitoring, and production operations.
Experience establishing engineering standards and reusable technical patterns across multiple teams.
Proven ability to influence technical direction across large organizations without relying on direct authority.
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical decisions to engineering and business leaders.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with modern cloud data platforms such as Microsoft Azure, Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, or equivalent technologies.
Experience with distributed data technologies such as Apache Spark, Kafka, Delta Lake, or comparable platforms.
Experience building data products using lakehouse, data mesh, or domain-oriented architecture patterns.
Experience implementing enterprise data governance, metadata management, lineage, data quality, and observability.
Experience building data foundations for machine learning, generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic AI.
Experience designing data services that expose governed enterprise data through APIs, event streams, semantic models, or AI-accessible interfaces.
Experience supporting large-scale operational environments where data freshness, accuracy, resiliency, and availability directly affect business operations.
Background in retail, hospitality, consumer services, or other large-scale distributed operational environments.

title: Accounts Receivable Analyst
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Finance Operations (FinOps) team provides and enhances core business services that are the backbone for Stripe. FinOps uses data and operational excellence to deliver technology solutions, procurement, billing and payroll services, strategic sourcing, and supplier relationship management to Stripe.
What you’ll do
We're looking for an Accounts Receivable (AR) Specialist to join our growing team. The AR Specialist will own billing and collections programs for Stripe’s growing mix of products that are invoiced. This role is responsible for projects within the end‑to‑end billing cycle, reconciliation of billing outputs to Finance reporting, and supporting AR collections strategy and improvement. The role works closely with Finance, Sales/GTM, Product, Data/Engineering, and Accounting to ensure invoices are accurate, timely, and collected.
Responsibilities
Own and execute defined Accounts Receivable (AR) programs and projects from planning through delivery, establishing scope, milestones, success measures, and accountability.
Develop and maintain project plans, track dependencies, and coordinate cross-functional execution to deliver agreed outcomes on time.
Translate AR business priorities into actionable workstreams, aligning stakeholders on requirements, deliverables, and ownership.
Proactively identify project risks, resolve execution blockers, and escalate decisions or trade-offs with clear recommendations.
Analyze AR performance and financial trends to identify gaps, investigate root causes, and recommend targeted improvements.
Partner with Finance, Sales/GTM, Engineering, and other stakeholders to deliver initiatives that improve receivables performance and the customer experience.
Lead process improvement projects that standardize and simplify AR workflows, reduce manual effort, and strengthen controls.
Gather business requirements and coordinate the prioritization, testing, and rollout of enhancements in partnership with technical teams.
Drive change management for assigned initiatives, including stakeholder communications, documentation, adoption planning, and post-launch measurement.
Define and monitor program metrics and leading indicators to measure business performance, delivery progress, and realized benefits.
Provide concise updates to AR and Finance leadership on program health, milestones, risks, decisions, and results.
Maintain program documentation, decision logs, and ownership handoffs to support sustainable outcomes and continuous improvement.
Own and execute subsidiary AR integration projects, aligning stakeholders on requirements, milestones, and dependencies while driving process improvements to standardize workflows, strengthen controls, and improve scalability.
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
8+ years of relevant experience in billing/accounts receivable with usage-based billing platforms or complex SaaS billing systems.
Strong Excel/Sheets and SQL literacy; comfortable reading billing query outputs and reconciling to invoices.
Experience working with APIs, simple python scripts, or Retool automations preferred.
Familiarity with payment methods (ACH, wires, crypto/USDC, Stripe payment links) and cash application best practices.
Excellent attention to detail, organized, and able to manage a heavy month‑end cadence and ad hoc adjustments.
Strong communication skills and ability to partner cross‑functionally (Sales, Finance, Data, Product, Legal).
A proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with business partners
A proven ability to be a self starter capable of driving business results without significant supervision
The ability to maintain high performance under tight timelines and a “roll up your sleeves” mindset to get any job done
The ability to bring structure to ambiguous areas of opportunity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment
Excellent problem-solving skills and demonstrated ability to work independently, analyze problems and data sets to make complex investigation decisions
Demonstrated history of taking on various types of challenging projects and producing results
Solution-oriented mindset with enthusiasm for establishing best practices
Self-disciplined, diligent, proactive and detail oriented

Thousands of developers and enterprises depend on it to operationalize LLMs across research, product, and production workloads.
The security surface spans API key and provider credential management across cloud boundaries, user prompt data flowing through the routing layer, a billing pipeline processing billions of daily events with financial-grade accuracy requirements, and an authentication layer federating external identity providers. What you'll do
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You manage a fast growing team of software and security engineers and make outsized impact through technical depth. Your focus will be cloud security infrastructure and modern AI development practices.  This is a player/coach role: you’ll establish the roadmap and grow the team while continuing to design systems, write code, evaluate tools, and work through difficult technical problems.
Own the security architecture. Threat-model the edge compute layer, provider integration surface, credential management system, billing pipeline, and analytics store. Make the architecture decisions — API key lifecycle, secrets rotation, data classification, auth enforcement — and partner with product and infra teams through implementation.
Secure the credential layer. Design and implement controls for API key issuance, rotation, revocation, and abuse detection across user-facing keys and upstream provider credentials spanning multiple secrets engines and cloud boundaries. This is the highest-risk surface on the platform and requires deep expertise in cryptographic credential management, OAuth/OIDC federation, and token-based access control.
Build detection and response. Instrument the platform for security events across edge, async processing, and database tiers. Build alerting, runbooks, and forensic tooling. Lead incident response when it matters. You own time-to-detect and time-to-contain, not just the playbook.
Integrate the platform into Stripe's security programs. Bring the platform into SecRev, vulnerability management, and incident response processes. Adapt controls designed for Stripe's primary infrastructure to fit an edge-first, multi-cloud architecture. Bridge Stripe's compliance frameworks (SOC 2, PCI DSS) with a platform that routes data across external providers.
Lead and develop the team. Manage existing team members and help rapidly scale it, in line with business and technical needs. Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and develop people.

You’re an engineer and a people leader who is comfortable representing the security posture to executive leadership . Software & security engineering depth. 10+ years in software engineering with deep expertise in at least two of: API security architecture, credential and secrets management, cloud security (IAM, network segmentation, encryption), or application security for high-throughput distributed systems.

Multi-cloud and edge security. Experience securing workloads that span multiple cloud providers or edge compute platforms: secrets management across trust boundaries, data classification for data in transit, and compliance in environments where you do not control the full stack.
Team leadership. Experience managing and growing a team of engineers, setting high expectations, and developing people. You have led teams where the quality of the work depended on your technical judgment, not just your organizational skills.
Communication. You explain security risks, architecture decisions, and compliance tradeoffs clearly to engineering, product, and executive audiences.
Thrives with ambiguity. A resourceful, pragmatic approach to execution: you can prioritize under constraints, make clear build-versus-buy decisions, and deliver useful improvements without waiting for perfect information.

title: Calibration, Localization and Mapping System Safety Engineer
description:
Zoox is on an ambitious journey to develop a full-stack autonomous mobility solution for cities and deploy such a robotaxi solution safely and reliably. The System Design and Mission Assurance (SDMA) team plays a foundational role in the company's success, responsible for constructing the safety case and fail-operational design for our autonomous driving robots before public road deployment. We are seeking a System Safety Engineer to perform safety analyses of complex hardware and software systems, specifically calibration, localization and mapping Systems. You will work across hardware and software domains to develop comprehensive system safety requirements and metrics that ensure safe, fail operational and reliable calibration, localization and mapping capabilities for our autonomous vehicle platform. This work is critical for scaling autonomous driving in a safe and reliable way.   • Work with partner teams to develop safe, fail operational, and cost-optimized solutions for problems in the calibration, localization and mapping domains

  • 6+ years of hands-on systems, safety, or related engineering experience with a focus on analysis of safety critical high-integrity systems in Automotive, ADAS, Autonomous vehicles, Aerospace or Robotics industries

  • Effective communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Apply industrial communications protocols, including Ethernet/IP, Modbus, and RS-485, and coordinate interfaces with corporate and industrial network architecture.

Validate CygNet configuration, communications, point-to-point mapping, alarm setpoints, shutdown setpoints, trends, and required operating displays for changes made to the facility during the project.

Experience with Allen Bradley PLC programming, RSLogix 5000, Studio 5000
